title: Coles Flybuys
body:
O.P.
http://www.theage.com.au/bus iness/coles-opens-new-front- in-supermarket-wars-20120419-1x8s8.html
Looks like there will finally be a loyalty program worth using, as Coles has just announced some changes to Flybuys and will be mailing out over 8 million cards to nearly every household in Australia.
My favourite part is 'My5', which apparently lets you choose 5 products of your choice from a list and get 10% off them. You also get one point for every dollar spent. Sounds pretty good to me and way better than current Flybuys or Everyday Rewards. What do people think?

---- replies ----
[User #21375422889 postsDaft VaderXBL: Daft Vader v2Whirlpool Forums Addict] Dr Van Nostrand writes...
You also get one point for every dollar spent. Sounds pretty good to me and way better than current Flybuys or Everyday Rewards.
For the everyday rewards I get one point for every dollar I spend at Woolies when I use my Woolies credit card plus another point for every dollar that is $30 or greater.
[User #522054289 postsBrian WhiteWhirlpool Forums Addict] Daft Vader writes...
For the everyday rewards I get one point for every dollar I spend at Woolies when I use my Woolies credit card plus another point for every dollar that is $30 or greater.
I have Everyday money and I get 3 points in Woolies store, 2 points at Woolies fuel and 1 point for all other purchases. (Per dollar spent).
I get a $25 shopper card every 5000 points. It suits me, i just dont trust Frequent flyer schemes in general.
[User #239457705 postsWhat? No VTECWhirlpool Enthusiast] I'm surprised they didn't do a deal with Virgin Australia like what Woolworths did.
Flybuys is still a scam though.
[User #4168362790 postsOZJetWhirlpool Forums Addict] This new FlyBuys scheme that launches Mon 23/4 is far better. Might end with a reward. I shop at Coles for convience very close to home (short walk). Also 9/10 I get petroll at Colse/Shell Express is its convient and I have 12c of from Coles Insurance.
Old scheme points expried in 3 years and Coles/Kmart/Traget 2 points for every $5 & coles Express 1 point for every $5.
New system Coles/Kmart/Target 1 point per $1 & Coles Express 1 point per every $2 & points dont expire. Plus this My5 10% off promo till Oct.
http://www.flybuys.com.au/
Looks far better than b4 plus its a free rewards scheme. Nearly all the very best rewards schemes cost $$$ & the better they are annual cost for scheme is targeted accordingly.
[User #8767613598 postsargamondWhirlpool Forums Addict] What, No VTEC? writes...
I'm surprised they didn't do a deal with Virgin Australia like what Woolworths did.
Flybuys is still a scam though.
Why is it a scam? What do you lose by using it?
[User #4168362790 postsOZJetWhirlpool Forums Addict] argamond writes...
Why is it a scam? What do you lose by using it?
No scam IMO but the old scheme was basically worthless without certain linked C/Cs that boosted rewards. I dont shope at Coles for FlyBuy points I shop as its the most convient for me. Plus no Costco or Aldi in Adelaide. It's not a scam but it's clear that Westfarmers want your business to be via the Coles Group basically. Having said that if you dont chase thee rewards and your norammly spending habits/stores you visit remain but you now can redem a gift card faster that a win IMO.
[User #4168362790 postsOZJetWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
Tender Prey writes...
I gave up on Fly Buys after taking 2 years to earn a $20 Target voucher.
I have a family member that has her linked Colesmastercard to FlyBuys scheme (no annual fee ever) as she is grandfathered. In the last year she has redemeed 5x$20 coles gif cards without changing her spending habbits. So the old flybuys program can work but without a CC to boost points its almost worthless. New scheme does look far better.
[User #117046604 postsBoredaussieWhy are we here?Whirlpool Enthusiast] Have a look at the fine print of the my5 stuff though. https://www.flybuys.com.au/w wwbusy/my5_interim_page.html You have to spend at least $50 in a transaction for the discount to apply. I don't think it's as good as it initially appears to be.
[User #8767613598 postsargamondWhirlpool Forums Addict] Boredaussie writes...
You have to spend at least $50 in a transaction for the discount to apply. I don't think it's as good as it initially appears to be.
Its a free bonus. Besides, my wife buys a ~$80/kg cheese (~150g each) so that we are quite a bit of the way there. Its also exciting as I have been looking to replace my visa credit card, and the source card was tempting with its 60 days interest free. With a good rewards program, would be even more enticing...
[User #4168362790 postsOZJetWhirlpool Forums Addict] Just noticed that while the new flybuys scheme is better that they jacked up the number if points needed for a reward. For example under old system needed 1250 points for $10 off reward coles mastercard, now it's 2000 points for same reward (as per close matercard website). Flybuys website is not live till Monday but it use to be 2500 points for $20 giftcard so given the above I bet it's now 4000 point's. Still better than old scheme but the give it in one hand and take some of it back in the other.
[User #486815183 postsH.F.M.2Participant] I never really cared too much for rewards cards, call my cynical but the cards are always going to be to the benefit of Coles, not the consumer. Reward me all you like but I hope I'm not paying for the rewards in the end.
[User #4168362790 postsOZJetWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
I here you and there is some truth in that for sure. However given there is no Aldi & Costco in Adelaide and I dont change my spending habbits or stores I shop at the chase rewards & I can walk to Coles. A "free" rewards program that now offers more in terms of being able to redeem get something for nothing per se.
[User #2441273277 posts2010daveNo longer useWhirlpool Forums Addict] Sending cards to almost every Australian home when only a fraction of them want to use the scheme sounds environmentally irresponsible.
What's the point of bothering to recycle if the Coles marketing department is going to waste all that plastic and paper for something most people will throw in the bin
[User #4623595999 postsGunk'N'StuffWho needs a quipWhirlpool Forums Addict] JJthejetplane writes...
For example under old system needed 1250 points for $10 off reward coles mastercard, now it's 2000 points for same reward (as per close matercard website)
BUt comparing the amount of points you can earn at Coles, Kmart, Target etc. (1-$1 vs 2-$5) it'll take you less money to get the rewards, all other things being the same. 1250 points under the old points system would cost 3125 dollars vs 2000 points only costing $2000. So they are giving out more than they are taking away with this new system, assuming there is no hidden catch.
[User #131402801 postsDJ Kingwide world of whatWhirlpool Forums Addict] can you still use the old flybuys cards and still get $1 = 1 point? (and will linked cards still work?)
